`mail.expunge`, `mail.append`, `mail.send`, `pim.edit`, `pim.respond`.

switches.description: The instance switches from the config.

capabilities.description: Every capability to have on; the rest are turned off.

AccountDto.description: A mail account of an archive.

oneOf.description: How an IMAP account connects; `null` for other kinds and for members.

Whether its contacts and calendars are archived; `null` for accounts that cannot have
them yet (import accounts; Microsoft accounts until Microsoft Graph contacts arrive).
How a JMAP account connects; `null` for other kinds and for members.

min_age_days.description:
Only messages at least this many days old are archived; younger ones wait for a later
sync. `null` archives every message.

needs_sign_in.description:
Someone has to sign in again: the provider no longer accepts the sign-in (it does not sync
until then), or sending or changing mail needs consent the sign-in lacks
(`sign_in_reason` says so; it keeps syncing).

oauth_provider.description: `google` or `microsoft` when it signs in with OAuth; `null` for a password.

sign_in_reason.description: Why signing in again is needed when the sign-in itself still works; `null` otherwise.

suggested_authserv_id.description:
The authserv-id that stamps nearly all of this account's recent mail, offered for
`trusted_authserv_ids` while that list is empty; never used for trust on its own. `null`
when there is none, for import accounts and for members.

sync_interval_minutes.description: Its own minutes between syncs, 0 for only on request; `null` follows the server's.

trusted_authserv_ids.description:
The authentication servers whose `Authentication-Results` fields decide sender trust for
mail found in this account, in order; `null` for import accounts and for members.

oneOf.description: Which folders are watched for changes; `null` for import accounts and for members.

writable.description:
The mailbox capabilities (`mail.flags`, `mail.move`, `mail.delete`, `mail.expunge`,
`mail.append`) the current user may use on this account now: the instance switch, the
account's capability, the grant and the credentials' scope all allow it. Filled in the
archive's account list; empty in other answers. Every change is checked again when it is
asked for.

AccountStatusDto.description: What is happening to an account now and how its last sync or import ended.

oneOf.description: The latest contacts and calendars sync; `null` when there was none.

contacts_watch.description: The watch on its contacts and calendars.

finished_at.description: When the last run ended, Unix milliseconds.

new_messages.description: Messages added by the running or last run.

next_sync_at.description: When the scheduler syncs it next, Unix milliseconds; `null` when it does not.

running.description: A sync or import is running.

AccountUpdateRequest.description: Changes to an account; missing fields stay as they are.

oneOf.description:
A new server, user name and excluded folders; checked by signing in, with `password`
when given and the stored one otherwise. Another host or port, or a move to `plain`,
needs `password`; OAuth accounts keep their server, port and security.
Turn archiving contacts and calendars on or off.

contacts_interval_minutes.description:
Minutes between contacts and calendars syncs, 0 for only on request; `null` follows the
mail interval again. Missing keeps it.

min_age_days.description:
Archive only messages at least this many days old, 1 to 3650; `null` or 0 archives every
message. Missing keeps it.

password.description:
A new password, or a new token for a JMAP account that signs in with one; checked by
signing in before it is stored.

sync_interval_minutes.description:
Its own minutes between syncs, 0 for only on request; `null` follows the server's again.
Missing keeps it.

trusted_authserv_ids.description:
Replaces the trusted authentication servers: at most 16 ids, each 1 to 255 printable
ASCII characters without spaces, trimmed, duplicates (ignoring case) dropped, order kept.
Trust them only when the server strips forged fields with its id. Not for import accounts.

oneOf.description: Which folders are watched for changes.

AddressDto.description: One mailbox of an address header.

AddressPersonDto.description: An address that belongs to a person.

email.description: The address as the message writes it.

has_card.description:
The person has a contact card that is not removed, as opposed to being known from mail
alone.

AlarmFormDto.description: A reminder before an event starts.

minutes_before.description: Minutes before the start; 0 at the start.

AliasAccountDto.description: An account receiving an alias's mail.

AliasDomainDto.description: A domain or suffix for new aliases.

accounts.description: Accounts its mail was archived from, most first.

created_at.description: Unix milliseconds of when the service made it.

mailboxes.description: Addresses the service forwards it to.

messages.description: Archived messages forwarded or addressed to it.

reply_strategy.description: How replies to its mail are sent: `reverse_alias`, `direct` or `reply_header`.

reply_strategy_source.description: `alias`, `domain` or `service` for an override, `default` for the detector's.

signed.description: Forwarded messages with the provider's passing signature.

source.description:
`service`: listed by a connected service; `manual`: added by hand; `mail`: only seen in
mail.

AliasListDto.description: The aliases and alias services of an archive.

AliasMailboxDto.description: A mailbox an alias can forward to.

AliasOptionsDto.description: Choices for a new alias at a service.

AliasProviderDto.description: An alias service the server knows.

oneOf.description: What its API can do; `null` when it has none.

AliasServiceDto.description: An account at an alias service.

oneOf.description: What its API can do.

synced_at.description: Unix milliseconds of the last listing.

AliasServiceUpdateRequest.description: Changes a service; missing fields stay.

AliasStrategiesDto.description: How replies to mail received through aliases are sent in an archive.

defaults.description: The default of every provider the server knows.

overrides.description:
Overrides, most specific scope first, then by key. An alias uses the override for its
address, else for its domain, else for its provider, else its provider's default.

key.description: The alias address, the domain or the provider id, lowercase.

AliasStrategyRequest.description: An override to set or, with `strategy` `null`, remove.

key.description: An alias address for `alias`, a domain for `domain`, a provider id for `service`.

AliasUpdateRequest.description: Changes an alias; missing fields stay, an empty string clears.

rights.description: What the current user may do in it.

save_remote_images.description: Remote images linked from its messages are downloaded and kept with the archive.

ArchiveRightsDto.description: The current user's rights in an archive, as the server checks them now.

compose.description:
Whether the user may write drafts and send here: the server sends mail, the `[write]`
switches allow sending, the grant is `sender`, the credentials carry `send:mail` and the
user may send as at least one active identity of the archive. Each send is still checked
against the transport and its account.

manage.description: Whether the user manages the archive: accounts, capabilities, transports and identities.

role.description: The user's grant: `reader`, `editor` or `sender`; each includes the ones before it.

save_remote_images.description:
Download remote images of its messages and keep them with the archive. Turning it on
starts saving the images of messages already archived.

thumbnail_url.description:
Where to get a small preview image, for PNG, JPEG, GIF and WebP images. The preview can
still be missing (`404`) when the image does not decode.

AuditEntryDto.description: One recorded write: ids and counts only.

user.description: The user who made it; missing for the server itself.

BoardingLegDto.description: One leg of a boarding pass.

flight.description: The flight number without the airline code.

BulkChangeRequest.description: The same change to many messages.

account.description: Only their places in this account.

CalendarOccurrenceDto.description: One instance of an event in a span, its copies folded together.

changed.description: Whether this instance was changed apart from its series.

collection_ids.description: The calendars of every copy, the leading one first.

copies.description: How many copies of this instance the shown calendars hold.

ends_at.description: End in UTC, Unix milliseconds; for dates the midnight after the last day.

floating.description: Times that read the same in every zone.

item_id.description: The leading copy: the highest `SEQUENCE`, then the latest `DTSTAMP` or `LAST-MODIFIED`.

recurrence_id.description:
The original start naming the instance, such as `2025-03-10T08:00:00Z` or `2025-03-10`;
absent for events that do not repeat.

removed.description: Whether every copy was removed from its source.

start_local.description: The start as a wall-clock time in its own zone, `2025-03-10T09:00:00` or `2025-03-10`.

starts_at.description:
Start in UTC, Unix milliseconds. Dates count from midnight UTC and floating times as if
they were UTC.

time_zone.description: The start's original zone; absent for dates and floating times.

CalendarRangeDto.description: The instances of a span and the calendars they come from.

calendars.description: Every calendar of the archive, removed ones too.

truncated.description: Whether instances were left out because there were too many.

CalendarSourceDto.description: A calendar of the archive, for the toggles of the calendar views.

account_name.description: The account it is read from; absent for imported files and once the account is gone.

color.description: The color its source gave it, as written.

from_mail.description: Whether it holds the events found in mail.

removed_at.description: When it was removed from its source, Unix milliseconds.

CapabilitiesDto.description: What an alias service API can do.

CategoriesDto.description: The taxonomy of an archive with message counts, in taxonomy order, zeros included.

topics.description:
`purchases`, `travel`, `finance`, `health`, `social`, `jobs`, `events`, `government`;
`health` only when asked for and turned on.

CategoryCountDto.description: How many messages have one kind or topic.

CategoryKindDto.description: The kind of a message: who sent it and how.

CategoryOverrideDto.description: A user's choice of kind, topics or both for every message of a sender.

created_at.description: Unix milliseconds when it was first made.

created_by.description: The user who first made it.

key.description: The address, or the registrable domain, lowercase with an A-label domain.

kind.description: The kind it sets; `null` keeps the derived kind.

topics.description:
The topics it sets, replacing the derived ones; `null` keeps the derived topics.
Sensitive topics apply only to aligned messages.

CategoryOverrideRequest.description: An override to store. It replaces the override with the same scope and key.

key.description:
An address, or a domain whose registrable domain is used (an address is accepted there
and its domain taken). Normalised: lowercase, A-label domain, no trailing dot.

kind.description: A kind name; missing or `null` keeps the derived kind.

topics.description:
Topic names, possibly empty; missing or `null` keeps the derived topics. At least one of
`kind` and `topics` is needed.

CategorySourceDto.description:
Which layer decided a kind or topic. A higher layer wins: `override` over `content` over
`domain` over `headers`.

CategoryTopicDto.description: One topic of a message: what it is about.

oneOf.description:
Set on a topic of the override that the trust gate kept off this message; such a topic
does not apply to it. Absent on topics that apply.

ChangeDiffDto.description: A change next to the version it was made on and the latest upstream version.

base_version.description: The upstream version the change was made on; absent for a create.

fields.description:
The fields where the change or upstream differ from the base, in the order they first
appear. Alarms, client properties, `SEQUENCE`, `REV` and `UID` are left out.

latest_version.description: The latest upstream version; absent for a create that has not reached the account.

mine.description: The change's own iCalendar or vCard text; absent for a delete.

ChangeDto.description: One difference between a version and the one before it.

after.description: Absent when the value was removed.

before.description: Absent when the value was added.

field.description:
Such as `email`, `start`, or `instance 2025-03-17T09:00:00 Europe/Berlin summary` for a
changed instance of a recurring event.

ChangedInstanceDto.description: A changed or cancelled instance of a recurring event.

oneOf.description: The original start it replaces.

CollectionDto.description: An address book or a calendar.

account_id.description: The account it was read from; absent once that account was removed.

editable.description:
Whether the current user may create, change and delete its items now: it belongs to an
account, is not `read_only` and not removed, and every lock for `pim.edit` is open.

removed_at.description: When it was noticed gone from the source, Unix milliseconds; it stays readable.

synced_at.description:
When it was last synced from its server, Unix milliseconds; absent for imported files
and the calendar of events found in mail.

write_mode.description:
`read_only`, `held` (edits stay in Holtmail) or `write_through` (edits are sent to the
account).

ConfirmDto.description:
What a `message.sending` rule asked for a 409: the message waits for the sender's
confirmation.

reason.description: The rule's reason, shown to the sender.

ConnectionRequest.description: A new connection for an IMAP account, checked by signing in before it is stored.

ContactFormDto.description: The fields of the contact form. Saving it on an existing card rewrites only what changed.

full_name.description: Made from the name, the organization or the first address when absent.

uid.description: The `UID` of a new card; one is made when absent. Ignored for an existing card.

ContactsCalendarsDto.description: Whether and where an account's contacts and calendars are archived.

caldav_offer.description:
A CalDAV address that answered for a JMAP account without calendars; `null` otherwise,
and for members.

calendars_protocol.description:
How calendars are read, as `protocol`; `dav` with `protocol` `jmap` for a JMAP account
whose session offers no calendars.

calendars_url.description: Where calendars are read; `null` when not set, and for members.

contacts_url.description: Where address books are read; `null` when not set, and for members.

has_dav_password.description: CardDAV and CalDAV sign in with a password of their own.

interval_minutes.description: Minutes between their syncs, 0 for only on request; `null` follows the mail interval.

needs_consent.description:
A Google or Microsoft Graph account that has to sign in again to grant access to
contacts and calendars.

protocol.description:
How address books are read: `dav` (CardDAV at the address above), `graph` (Microsoft
Graph) or `jmap` (the JMAP account's own session).

ContactsCalendarsRequest.description: Turns archiving an account's contacts and calendars on or off.

calendars_url.description:
Where calendars are read. For a JMAP account whose session offers contacts but no
calendars, an address here alone (or none, when one is found) reads calendars over
CalDAV while contacts stay on JMAP.

contacts_url.description:
Where address books are read: a server such as `https://carddav.fastmail.com`, a DAV
root such as `https://cloud.example.com/remote.php/dav`, or one address book. With
neither address, they are detected from the account's address; with one, it serves both.
Ignored for Google accounts, which use Google's addresses, and Graph accounts, which use
Graph. A JMAP account without an address reads them through its JMAP session when that
offers contacts.

dav_password.description:
A password for CardDAV and CalDAV when the account's own does not work there, such as
an app password; never returned. Empty removes a stored one.

enabled.description:
Turning on signs in to the contacts and calendars server before anything is stored
(Google and Microsoft Graph accounts instead wait for their next sign-in); turning off
keeps what is archived.

ContactsCalendarsRunDto.description: The latest sync of an account's contacts and calendars.

summary.description: What it did, with counts only.

CopyAnswerDto.description: One copy's answer of an attendee.

status.description: Lowercase `PARTSTAT`; absent when the copy does not list them or has no answer.

CopyDifferenceDto.description: A field whose value differs between copies.

field.description:
Such as `start`, `location` or `attendee`; prefixed `instance <RECURRENCE-ID> ` for a
changed instance.

CopyValuesDto.description: One copy's values of a field that differs between copies.

values.description: Empty when the copy has no value.

CorrespondenceDto.description: What the mail says about a person: every message with one of their addresses, each once.

attachments.description: The newest first, at most 12; calendar parts are left out.

threads.description: The most recently active conversations first, at most 20.

CreateAliasRequest.description: Creates an alias at a service. Without `prefix` the service picks it.

domain.description: A domain id from the options.

archives.description: The archives JMAP and DAV may see; missing or `null` means every archive the user can read.

implicit_seen.description: Whether fetching a whole body marks a message read; off when missing.

mail_archive.description: The archive IMAP and SMTP serve; required with either protocol.

name.description: Shown in lists and audit entries; 1 to 100 characters.

scopes.description:
Any of `read`, `write:mail`, `send:mail`, `write:pim` and `notify`, at least one;
`["read"]` when missing.

CreatedDeviceDto.description: A device that was just made, with its app password.

secret.description: The app password: `hm_` plus 32 characters. Shown only here, once.

DataFileDto.description: One category data table the server uses.

attribution.description: The attribution to show with the data, when its licence asks for one.

license.description: The SPDX identifier of the data licence.

DataOriginDto.description: Where a data file came from.

DataOutcomeDto.description: The outcome of the last check for new category data.

DataUpdatesDto.description: Whether the server looks for new category data.

data_sources.description: The downloaded tables the server uses, by name.

enabled.description: `[insights.categories] update`, and the server runs the check.

last_checked_at.description: Unix milliseconds of the last check; `null` before the first.

oneOf.description: What the last check found; `null` before the first.

DefaultIdentityRequest.description: The current user's default identity in an archive.

identity.description: An identity the user may send as; `null` clears the default.

count.description: The review's `count`, typed again by the person deleting.

DeletionRequest.description: What to delete: a search or a list of messages, exactly one of them.

message_ids.description: Message ids; those not in the archive are left out.

query.description: A search as the search box reads it, e.g. `from:news@example.com before:2020-01-01`.

DeletionReviewDto.description: A frozen list of messages waiting to be deleted.

count.description: Messages it deletes; the confirmation repeats this number.

expires_at.description: Unix milliseconds; after this the review cannot be confirmed.

sample.description: Up to 20 of them, newest first.

DeletionSampleDto.description: One of the messages a deletion would remove.

DeliveryDto.description: One delivery of an event to a webhook.

event_id.description: The `id` in the body and the `Holtmail-Delivery` header.

next_at.description: Unix milliseconds of the next attempt; `null` once delivered or given up.

DeviceDto.description: A device: one client installation with its own app password.

archives.description: The archives JMAP and DAV may see; `null` means every archive the user can read.

has_secret.description: Whether it has an app password. The password itself is never shown again.

implicit_seen.description: Whether fetching a whole body marks a message read.

last_protocol.description: The protocol of its latest use.

last_used_day.description: Unix milliseconds of the start (UTC) of the last day it was used.

mail_archive.description: The archive IMAP and SMTP serve to it.

raised_at.description: Unix milliseconds of the last raise of its rights after it was made.

revoked_at.description: Unix milliseconds of its revocation, which is permanent.

DeviceServerDto.description: One place a device can connect to.

host.description: The name to connect to; `null` when the server has no name of its own to give.

url.description: For `jmap` and `dav`: the full address to give the client; absent for IMAP and SMTP.

DeviceSetupDto.description: What this server offers to devices.

apple_profile.description: Whether `POST /api/devices/{id}/profile` can make an Apple profile on this server.

autoconfig.description:
The mail domains Thunderbird finds this server for by itself from an address; empty
when autoconfig answers for none.

can_create.description: Whether this user may make devices and raise their rights.

davx5.description:
The link that opens DAVx5 with this server and the user's login filled in; `null` unless
DAV is served over https. It never carries a password.

servers.description: The configured listeners, implicit TLS first; empty when none is.

DraftAttachment.description:
A file of a draft. Stored drafts always carry `blob`, `name`, `content_type` and `size`.
When saving, an attachment is either one the draft already has (`blob`) or an attachment of
an archived message (`message` and `ordinal`), which the server resolves.

content_id.description: For a part the HTML shows through `cid:`.

DraftContext.description: What the draft answers or forwards; used to pick the identity.

message.description: The archived message it answers or forwards.

reverse_alias.description:
A reverse alias the server made for the original's sender when the draft was started,
so the route can show it; sending makes or asks for it again.

reverse_contacts.description:
Reverse aliases the server made for other recipients (the `use_reverse_alias` fix).
Sending asks the alias service again and trusts only those it confirms.

DraftDto.description: A draft at its newest version, with the route it would take now.

leaks.description:
Recipients that would see the real mailbox behind an alias; sending refuses while any
is left unless told to send anyway.

version.description: Grows by one with every save; send it back to save again.

identity.description: The identity picked by hand; `null` lets the route decide.

send_at.description: When to send, Unix milliseconds; `null` for as soon as the undo window ends.

DraftSaveRequest.description: A new version of a draft.

version.description: The version this one replaces; another save in between answers `409`.

DraftVersionDto.description: One kept version of a draft.

DroppedLocalFlagsDto.description: How many messages had their local flags dropped.

EventCopyDto.description: One copy of an event: an item in a calendar.

from_mail.description: Whether it is the event as the archived mail describes it.

leading.description: Whether it is the copy the event is shown from.

removed_at.description: When the copy, or its calendar, was removed from its source, Unix milliseconds.

stamp.description: The later of `DTSTAMP` and `LAST-MODIFIED`, Unix milliseconds.

EventDetailDto.description: Everything about one event and its copies.

attendees.description: Everyone any copy lists, in the order they first appear.

copies.description: The leading copy first, then by rank.

differences.description: Fields whose values differ between the copies.

messages.description: Messages any copy's versions came in, oldest first.

timeline.description: Every version of every copy, oldest first.

viewer_zone.description: The viewer's zone the `in_zone` times are in, when it names a known zone.

EventFormDto.description: The fields of the event form. Saving it on an existing event rewrites only what changed.

end.description: Like `start`, exclusive for all-day events; absent means one day or one hour.

start.description: `YYYY-MM-DD` for an all-day event, else `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]` in `time_zone`.

time_zone.description: `UTC`, an IANA or Windows zone name; absent for a floating time.

uid.description: The `UID` of a new event; one is made when absent. Ignored for an existing event.

in_zone.description:
The wall-clock time in the viewer's zone (`tz`), such as `2025-03-10T09:00:00`; absent for
dates, floating times and without `tz`.

EventMomentDto.description: A time of the event as written, and in the zone the viewer asked for.

EventPersonDto.description: An organizer or attendee, linked to a person when one has their address.

answers.description: Their answer in each copy, in the order of `copies`; empty for the organizer.

status.description: Their answer in the leading copy, lowercase.

EventTimeDto.description: A time of an event: as written, in its zone, and in UTC.

time_zone.description:
The original zone: a `TZID` such as `Europe/Berlin`, `UTC`, an offset, or absent for
floating times and dates.

value.description:
As written: `2025-03-10` for a date, `2025-03-10T09:00:00` for a time, with `Z` or an
offset when written so.

at.description:
When it happened: the date of the first message it came in, else when it was first seen.
Unix milliseconds.

EventVersionDto.description: A version of one copy, on the event's merged timeline.

FieldDiffDto.description: One field of a change compared with its base and the latest upstream version.

base.description: Its values in the version the change was made on; empty when it had none.

conflict.description: Both differ from the base, and from each other.

field.description:
The field as the item history names it, such as `summary`, `start`, `attendee`, `email`
or `instance 2026-12-01T10:00:00 Europe/Berlin summary`.

mine_changed.description: The change differs from the base here.

theirs.description: Its values in the latest upstream version; empty when the item is gone upstream.

theirs_changed.description: Upstream differs from the base here.

FieldValueDto.description: One value of a person's field.

value.description: As the first card that says it writes it.

mode.description: `test`, `on` or `off`; any mode clears a pause.

FlowDto.description: A flow of an archive as of its current version.

mode.description: `test` (runs are logged, nothing is carried out; new flows start here), `on` or `off`.

paused.description:
Set while the circuit breaker holds the flow (`circuit_breaker`); setting a mode clears
it.

paused_at.description: When it was paused, Unix milliseconds.

position.description: Place in the archive's order, from 0; flows run in this order and `stop` ends the chain.

saved_by.description: Who saved the current version; the flow's actions are limited by their rights.

trigger.description: The trigger type of the current version.

FlowIssuesDto.description: Why a flow was refused: every issue the validator found.

FlowRunDto.description: One run in the runs log.

results.description: What became of each planned action, in plan order.

test.description: Evaluated only: the flow was in test mode.

error.description: Why nothing could be planned; the plan is empty then.

plan.description: The plan: `ran`, `ignored`, `path` (each node with its outcome), `actions`, `stopped`.

FlowTestRequest.description: A dry run: what the flow would do for an event, nothing carried out or logged.

at.description: When the event happens, Unix milliseconds; now by default.

flow.description: An unsaved flow to test instead of the saved one (required for the archive-wide test).

live.description: Treat the message as live mail (default `true`).

message.description: The message the event is about.

FolderDto.description: A folder with its message count.

name.description: The last level of the path.

unread.description: Messages in the folder without the `\Seen` flag there.

ForwardRequest.description: A forward of an archived message.

GrantDto.description: One archive granted to a user.

role.description: `reader`, `editor` or `sender`; each includes the ones before it.

GrantRequest.description: A user's grant on an archive.

role.description: `reader`, `editor` or `sender`. Only the owner gives `editor` and `sender`.

HeldBackDto.description: Why a topic of an override does not apply to this message.

IdentityDto.description: An address people may send as.

default.description: Whether it is the current user's default in the archive.

oneOf.description:
Set when the provider sent mail as this identity with another `From`, as its synced
Sent copy showed; `null` otherwise.

users.description: Users who may send as it.

IdentityRequest.description:
An identity to add. It starts inactive unless `active` is set, and becomes active only when
its transport may send as the address and the transport check passes.

sent_copy.description:
`provider`, `append:<folder>` or `none`; `provider` for account transports and `none`
otherwise when missing.

transport.description: The transport: the archive's own or an instance transport granted to it.

IdentitySuggestionDto.description: An address that could become an identity.

source.description:
`account` (an account's address), `alias` (the alias store) or `sent` (a sender of the
archive's sent mail).

transport.description: A transport that may send as the address, when the archive has one.

IdentityUpdateRequest.description: Changes to an identity; missing fields stay as they are, empty strings clear optional ones.

IdentityUsersRequest.description: Who may send as an identity.

ImageProxyDto.description: The outbound proxy for remote images.

from_config.description: Set in the server's config; the API cannot change it.
